

```{r setup, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Send knitr's per-chunk plot files to a temporary directory so knitting never
# creates a `figure/` folder in the project tree. The figures committed to the
# repo are written separately by the explicit ggsave2() calls into figures/.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE,
                      fig.path = file.path(tempdir(), "knitr-fig/"))

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)

my_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 19) +
  theme(
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = 'transparent', colour = NA),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = 'transparent', colour = NA),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = 'transparent'),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = 'transparent'),
    legend.position   = "none"
  )

label_size <- 6   # for geom_text() (ggplot's geom size ~= mm, not pt)

source(here::here('code/source_scripts/01_functions.R'))

```

#Data Request Figures:

## Increasing number of DR

```{r slide2}

my_pal <- scales::seq_gradient_pal(low = "#00affa", high = "#004f71", space = "Lab")

colors <- my_pal(seq(0,1, length.out = length(unique(requests$approved_year))))
p1 <- requests %>%
  select(vivli_id, approved_year) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .by = approved_year) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(approved_year = factor(year(approved_year), levels = c("2018", "2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025"))) %>%
  arrange(approved_year) %>%
  mutate(cum_growth = cumsum(count)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = approved_year, y = cum_growth, fill = approved_year)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(y = cum_growth+30, label = cum_growth), size = label_size) +
 # labs(title = "Cumulative Number of Approved Data Requests Since Dec-2018",
 #      subtitle = paste0("(", requests_n, " total approved requests from Dec-2018 to Dec-2025)")) +
  xlab("Year") +
  ylab("Data Requests (n)") +
  my_theme +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors)


  p1
```

## Cumulative publications by type

```{r slide4}

# Colorblind-safe categorical palette for the publication types (panel E legend)
pub_levels <- c("Journal Article", "Abstract", "Preprint", "Letter",
                "Review", "Thesis/Dissertation", "Repository")
pub_colors <- c("Journal Article" = "#0072B2", "Abstract" = "#E69F00",
                "Preprint" = "#009E73", "Letter" = "#CC79A7",
                "Review" = "#56B4E9", "Thesis/Dissertation" = "#D55E00",
                "Repository" = "#F0E442")

p3 <- disclosures %>%
  select(public_disclosure, metrics_year, pub_type_vivli) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(pub_type_vivli)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(metrics_year = factor(metrics_year, levels = c(2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)),
                pub_type_vivli = factor(pub_type_vivli, levels = pub_levels)) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .by = c(metrics_year, pub_type_vivli)) %>%
  # Fill every year x publication-type combination with 0 so each type's
  # cumulative carries forward across years with no new publications. This
  # keeps Repository (1 in 2024, 0 in 2025) visible as a cumulative 1 in 2025,
  # and makes the per-year total (cum_growth) the true cumulative every year.
  tidyr::complete(metrics_year, pub_type_vivli, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  arrange(metrics_year) %>%
  group_by(pub_type_vivli) %>%
  mutate(cum_types = cumsum(count)) %>%
  group_by(metrics_year) %>%
  mutate(cum_growth = sum(cum_types)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = metrics_year, y = cum_types, fill = pub_type_vivli)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(y = cum_growth+20, label = cum_growth), size = label_size) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pub_colors, drop = FALSE, name = "Publication type") +
  xlab("Year") +
  ylab("Publications (n)") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm")) +
  guides(size = "none", fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3))

p3
```

#### Outcomes

```{r}
journal_articles_n <- nrow(subset(disclosures, pub_type_vivli == "Journal Article"))

my_pal <- scales::seq_gradient_pal(high = "#00affa", low = "#004f71", space = "Lab")

colors <- my_pal(seq(0,1, length.out = 8))


p4 <- disclosures %>%
  dplyr::filter(pub_type_vivli == "Journal Article") %>%
  dplyr::select(public_disclosure, outcome_category) %>%
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(outcome_category, delim = ",") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(outcome_category = ifelse(outcome_category == "Supporting Future Research", "Informing patient-care decisions", outcome_category),
                outcome_category = ifelse(outcome_category == "Algorithm/Code", "Algorithm or Code", outcome_category)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.by = outcome_category,
                   count = n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(outcome_category, count), y = count,
             fill = reorder(outcome_category, count))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.2, size = label_size) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  xlab("Outcome category") +
  ylab("Journal articles (n)") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  my_theme

  p4

# Percentage of journal articles informing patient-care decisions (matches Figure 2D / panel F,
# which rolls "Supporting Future Research" into "Informing patient-care decisions")
patient_care_n <- disclosures %>%
  dplyr::filter(pub_type_vivli == "Journal Article") %>%
  dplyr::select(public_disclosure, outcome_category) %>%
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(outcome_category, delim = ",") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(outcome_category = ifelse(outcome_category == "Supporting Future Research", "Informing patient-care decisions", outcome_category)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::filter(outcome_category == "Informing patient-care decisions") %>%
  nrow()
print(paste0("Journal articles informing patient-care decisions: ", patient_care_n, " of ", journal_articles_n, " (", round(100 * patient_care_n / journal_articles_n), "%)"))
```

Combined manuscript figure

```{r}
gradient_blue <- function(n) scales::seq_gradient_pal(low = "#00affa", high = "#004f71",
                                                     space = "Lab")(seq(0, 1, length.out = n))

# Panel C: trials per data request by approval year (side-by-side bars)
trials_tab <- requests %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(studies_n)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(trial_bin = dplyr::case_when(
    studies_n == 1 ~ "1", studies_n == 2 ~ "2", studies_n == 3 ~ "3",
    studies_n == 4 ~ "4", studies_n == 5 ~ "5", TRUE ~ "6+"),
    trial_bin = factor(trial_bin, levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6+")),
    year = factor(lubridate::year(approved_year))) %>%
  dplyr::count(year, trial_bin)
pC <- ggplot(trials_tab, aes(x = year, y = n, fill = trial_bin)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gradient_blue(6), name = "Trials per request") +
  xlab("Year approved") +
  ylab("Data requests (n)") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

# Panel D: data contributors per data request by approval year (side-by-side bars)
contrib_tab <- requests %>%
  dplyr::mutate(contrib_bin = dplyr::case_when(
    data_contributor_n == 1 ~ "1", data_contributor_n == 2 ~ "2",
    data_contributor_n == 3 ~ "3", data_contributor_n == 4 ~ "4",
    TRUE ~ "5+"),
    contrib_bin = factor(contrib_bin, levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5+")),
    year = factor(lubridate::year(approved_year))) %>%
  dplyr::count(year, contrib_bin)
pD <- ggplot(contrib_tab, aes(x = year, y = n, fill = contrib_bin)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(preserve = "single")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gradient_blue(5), name = "Contributors per request") +
  xlab("Year approved") +
  ylab("Data requests (n)") +
  my_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))

# Panel F: distribution of approved data requests by therapeutic area (from
# requests.rds, the tracked approved-request population). One therapeutic area
# per request; blank and literal "N/A" collapse into "Unclassified".
collapse_ta_req <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "N/A", "Unclassified", x)
}
# Full, unlumped table: written to the panel-F data CSV (every therapeutic area).
ta_req_tab <- requests %>%
  dplyr::mutate(therapeutic_area = collapse_ta_req(therapeutic_area)) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.by = therapeutic_area, count = dplyr::n()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(count))

# Figure version only: show the 10 largest therapeutic areas and roll the rest
# into a single "Other" bar. "Other" is pinned to the bottom of the plot.
ta_top <- dplyr::slice_max(ta_req_tab, count, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)
ta_req_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ta_top,
  tibble::tibble(therapeutic_area = "Other",
                 count = sum(ta_req_tab$count) - sum(ta_top$count))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(therapeutic_area = factor(therapeutic_area,
                                          levels = c("Other", rev(ta_top$therapeutic_area))))
pF <- ggplot(ta_req_plot, aes(x = therapeutic_area, y = count, fill = therapeutic_area)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), hjust = -0.2, size = label_size - 1) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  xlab("Therapeutic area") +
  ylab("Data requests (n)") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gradient_blue(nrow(ta_req_plot))) +
  my_theme +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13))

# Six-panel layout:
#   A requests by year          B requests by therapeutic area
#   C trials per request        D contributors per request
#   E cumulative publications   F outcome categories
combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(p1, pF, pC, pD, p3, p4,
                   labels = LETTERS[1:6],
                   ncol = 2,
                   scale = 0.95,
                   align = "hv")
ggsave2(plot = combined,
                   filename = here::here("figures/manuscript_figure.tiff"),
        scale =3,
        width = 8.5,
        height= 8,
        bg='transparent')


ggsave2(plot = combined,
                   filename = here::here("figures/manuscript_figure.png"),
        scale =2,
        width = 8.5,
        height= 8,
        bg='transparent')

# Save each panel's underlying data alongside manuscript_figure.png (A-F match the
# panels). Panel B keeps the full, unlumped therapeutic-area table (all areas),
# even though the figure shows only the top 10 plus a combined "Other" bar.
readr::write_csv(p1$data, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_A_data.csv"))
readr::write_csv(ta_req_tab, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_B_data.csv"))
readr::write_csv(pC$data, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_C_data.csv"))
readr::write_csv(pD$data, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_D_data.csv"))
readr::write_csv(p3$data, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_E_data.csv"))
readr::write_csv(p4$data, here::here("figures/manuscript_figure_F_data.csv"))

```

## Studies and participants by therapeutic area

```{r study_therapeutic_area}
# One therapeutic area per study; combine blank and literal "N/A" into "Unclassified".
collapse_ta <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | x == "" | x == "N/A", "Unclassified", x)
}

ta_summary <- study_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(therapeutic_area = collapse_ta(`Therapeutic Areas`),
                participants = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`# Participants`))) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(.by = therapeutic_area,
                   studies = dplyr::n(),
                   participants = sum(participants, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(studies))

# Underlying data keeps every therapeutic area (no cutoff)
readr::write_csv(ta_summary, here::here("figures/study_therapeutic_area_data.csv"))

# The figure shows only therapeutic areas with at least 100 studies; all panels
# share the therapeutic-area order set by study count
ta_plot <- ta_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(studies >= 100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(therapeutic_area = factor(therapeutic_area, levels = rev(therapeutic_area)))

n_ta <- nrow(ta_plot)

# One horizontal-bar panel per metric, all sharing the study-count ordering
ta_panel <- function(yvar, ylab, show_axis, expand_r = 0.15) {
  p <- ggplot(ta_plot, aes(x = therapeutic_area, y = .data[[yvar]], fill = therapeutic_area)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(.data[[yvar]])), hjust = -0.15, size = label_size - 1) +
    coord_flip(clip = "off") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, expand_r)), labels = scales::comma) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = gradient_blue(n_ta)) +
    xlab(if (show_axis) "Therapeutic area" else NULL) + ylab(ylab) +
    my_theme +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 16, r = 6, b = 3, l = 3))
  if (!show_axis) p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  p
}

# A studies   B participants (shared therapeutic-area order)
pA_study <- ta_panel("studies", "Studies (n)", TRUE, expand_r = 0.20)
pB_study <- ta_panel("participants", "Participants (n)", FALSE, expand_r = 0.30)

study_figure <- cowplot::plot_grid(pA_study, pB_study, labels = c("A", "B"),
                                    ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1.83, 1), align = "h",
                                    label_y = 1, vjust = 1)

ggsave2(plot = study_figure,
        filename = here::here("figures/study_therapeutic_area.tiff"),
        scale = 1.3, width = 11, height = 6, bg = "transparent")
ggsave2(plot = study_figure,
        filename = here::here("figures/study_therapeutic_area.png"),
        scale = 1.1, width = 11, height = 6, bg = "transparent")

study_figure
```

## Public disclosures cited in policy documents

Policy citations are drawn from the Overton index of Vivli publications
(`data/Overton_index articles-2026-02-10.csv`). The full article-to-policy-document
detail is provided for reference as Supplemental Table 3
(`figures/Supplemental_Table_3_policy_citations.csv`).

```{r policy_citations}
# Policy citations come from the Overton index; match its article DOIs to our
# public disclosures so the table counts only disclosures included in this deposit.
overton <- readr::read_csv(here::here("data/Overton_index articles-2026-02-10.csv"),
                           show_col_types = FALSE)

norm_doi <- function(x) tolower(trimws(x))
disclosure_dois <- unique(norm_doi(disclosures$doi[!is.na(disclosures$doi) & disclosures$doi != ""]))

# One Overton row = one (article, policy document) citing pair
overton_matched <- overton %>%
  dplyr::mutate(doi = norm_doi(DOI)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(doi %in% disclosure_dois)

policy_citation_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("Public disclosures cited in >=1 policy document",
             "Policy documents citing a public disclosure",
             "Total public disclosure to policy document citations"),
  Count  = c(dplyr::n_distinct(overton_matched$doi),
             dplyr::n_distinct(overton_matched$`Document page`),
             nrow(overton_matched)))

readr::write_csv(policy_citation_table, here::here("figures/policy_citation_table.csv"))
knitr::kable(policy_citation_table)

# Supplemental Table 3: the Overton policy-citation index for Vivli publications,
# cleaned for reference (HTML tags stripped, article date parsed, working/ID and
# duplicate URL columns dropped). Readers are referred to this table for the full
# article-to-policy-document detail behind the counts above.
strip_html <- function(x) trimws(gsub("<[^>]+>", "", x))
supplemental_table_3 <- overton %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    `Article title`        = strip_html(Title),
    Journal                = Journal,
    DOI                    = DOI,
    `Article published`    = as.Date(`Published on`),
    `Policy organization`  = strip_html(`Cited by source`),
    `Policy document`      = strip_html(`Cited by title`),
    `Policy document date` = `Cited by date`,
    `Organization sector`  = `Cited by organisation sector`,
    `Organization type`    = `Cited by organisation type`,
    Country                = `Cited by country`,
    `Policy document URL`  = `Cited by URL`) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(`Article title`, `Policy organization`, `Policy document`)

readr::write_csv(supplemental_table_3,
                 here::here("figures/Supplemental_Table_3_policy_citations.csv"))
```
